profile.headline: Software Engineer @ Good Dog
profile.geoLocationName: New York, New York, United States
profile.summary:
I graduated from the Georgia Institute of Technology in May 2018. I studied Computer Science with a focus on People and Media. I am a Vermonter, so naturally I love hiking and maple syrup. I enjoy watching The Office, finding new coffee shops in NYC, and spending time with my family and friends.
I started full-time as a Software Engineer at JP Morgan in July 2018 on a team in the Wealth and Asset Management line of business doing full-stack development with a front-end in React/Typescript and back-end in Java. 
In November 2020 I joined Quio Technologies as a Frontend Engineer. Since then, I have been working on remote patient monitoring platforms primarily using React/Redux and Typescript. My passion for front-end development, user interface design, and working with my team to build creative solutions is growing everyday.
I love learning and actively expanding my skill set. I am grateful for the amazing opportunities that have come my way thus far and am excited to see what the future has in store.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.locationName: New York, New York, United States
positions.description: Skills: React.js · Ruby on Rails · JavaScript

positions.title: Technology Analyst Intern
positions.description: At this internship I got to collaborate and work closely with international team members almost daily. I developed a full-stack web app using Spring Boot and JP Morgan's internal Moneta framework for clients to view some of their financial information from inputted search criteria. I also built an app for senior management to make functionality requests for an existing app. I created and pushed a UI app to cloud to update senior management on my team’s projects in Wealth and Asset Management. These applications used HTML, CSS (Bootstrap), and AngularJS for front-end and Java for back-end.

positions.title: Biotechnology Seminar Participant
positions.description: I used and developed my skills in the field of biotechnology through research with professors. I tested whether or not the labels of several medications were accurate by performing a variety of tests on each drug. I collected specimen from a nearby river and decomposed them to analyze their DNA. Through centrifuging, gel electrophoresis, and matching DNA with previously discovered species using the BLAST computer program, I determined whether or not the species in the river were invasive.

honors.title: President's Award for Educational Achievement
honors.description: Grade point average of at least a 3.5 on a 4 point scale, top 10% of class, high achievement in reading or math on the SAT.
honors.issuer: Issued by U.S. Department of Education · Jun 2014

volunteerExperiences.description: Plan and execute annual summer camps that have over 7,000 participants in the Northeast region of the United States, taught 20 high school girls about several concepts regarding Hinduism through presentations weekly, created documents for others to present on based off of my own research, conduct monthly meetings and conference calls regarding project development, helping improve each year, market and coordinate special events with emails, posters, and other types of innovative ideas.

projects.title: Slash and Dash
projects.description: My team and I developed a travel web app that uses one of Amadeus's API at HackMIT. The app searches through ten years of flight information to find the best place to travel to for an affordable spontaneous trip. The app uses ReactJS, Node.js, and basic machine learning algorithms like clustering and linear regression between the flight cost and location of departure to help with cost-effective traveling.

projects.title: SafeWord
projects.description: My team and I are in the process of developing an android and iOS voice activated app. The app uses speech triggers to contact customized people through text or phone call. It has the possibility of sending GPS location as well. We work closely with our client to ensure the product is exactly what they are looking for. We have five Sprints this semester to create a completed application.

organizations.name: BAPS Campus Fellowship
organizations.description: Planned and organized Campus Diwali Celebration Event which has over 400 people in attendance and over 100 volunteers. Organized and presented in biweekly discussions which helped individuals stay connected to their culture on campus. Marketed and coordinated special events with flyers, emails and other types of innovative ideas.

organizations.name: Student Center Programs Council
organizations.position: Atlanta Life Committee Member, Concerts Committee Member, Internal Development Committee Member · Aug 2015 - Present
organizations.description: Organize several events throughout the year around Atlanta, GA for 5,500+ students and guests to attend.Deliberate methods of improving the relationships between members of the organization to increase efficiency and improve teamwork. Negotiate ticket pricing and funding with companies to enable the organization to subsidize tickets for the student body, making activities in the area more affordable for a college budget. Organize a free homecoming concert for the student body after negotiating contracts with musical performers and artists.
